title: theme_pomological_plain() Error. Font '' isn't in the extrafont font list...
description:
There is an error due to the font not being specified in theme_pomological_plain().

The error message looks like this.

```
> p + theme_pomological_plain() 
Warning message:
Font '' isn't in the extrafont font list (but it may still work). If recently installed, you can try running `extrafont::font_import()`. 
```

After reviewing the source code below, I believe that base_family = "" is the cause.

R > theme_pomological > Line 125~127

```
theme_pomological_plain <- function(base_family = "", base_size = 11, plot.background.color = "transparent", ...) {
  theme_pomological(base_family, base_size, plot.background.color = plot.background.color, ...)
}
```

Is this considered a problem?
Or is it a misconfiguration on my part?

thank you!

title: Doc suggestion (minor)
description:
Awesome package!

Just went through the examples in the readme. It's possible to save the plots as PDF with the following:

    #extrafont::font_import()  # run once after new fonts are installed
    extrafont::loadfonts()  # ggsave will not be able to use special font otherwise
    ggsave(plot = myplot, filename = "myplot.pdf")  # works if the previous line is run

Maybe worth mentioning in the readme?

I also found that saving to PNG as indicated in the readme did not give a good result when the resolution was set to a high value, but something like the following worked well (width and height need to be adjusted)

    paint_pomological(p_basic, res = 600, width = 2400, height = 1600) %>% 
      magick::image_write("ggpomological-basic-highres.png", quality = 100)

title: `ggpomological::paint_pomological` no longer working
description:
I am not sure if this has to do with me working on development versions of both `R` and `RStudio`, but I can no longer get the following example to run successfully on my machine:

# Reprex

``` r
# setup
set.seed(123)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggpomological)

# Prep msleep data
msleep <- ggplot2::msleep[, c("vore", "sleep_rem", "sleep_total")]
msleep <- msleep[complete.cases(msleep), ]
msleep$vore <- paste0(msleep$vore, "vore")

# Base plot
basic_msleep_plot <- ggplot(msleep) +
  aes(x = sleep_rem, y = sleep_total, color = vore) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  labs(color = NULL)

# With pomological theme
ggpomological::paint_pomological(pomo_gg = basic_msleep_plot)
#> Error in magick_device_internal(bg = bg, width = width, height = height, : Graphics API version mismatch
```

```r
library(ggimage) ## `geom_image`, `geom_subview` and `theme_transparent`

ggplot(d=data.frame(x=0:1, y=0:1), aes(x, y)) + 
    geom_image(image=ggpomological:::pomological_images("background"),size=Inf) + 
    geom_subview(subview= pomological_iris+ theme_transparent(), width=Inf, height=Inf, x=.5, y=.5) +
    theme_void()
```

The output is still `gg` object. 

PS: I am the author of `ggimage`.

title: modified base_theme?
description:
Hello,
first of all, thanks for this really cool package, I absolutely love it. My question might be more of a general R question than specific to your package, so I apologise if it doesn't fit here.
I have a document in which I mainly use the cow_plot package. 
Now, I have a specific instance where I wanted to use pomological, as follow. 

```
plot = ggplot(data = BA) + geom_line(aes(x = chromEnd, y = meanCoverage, color = facet))
ttle = paste0("**Coverage distribution", " before and after repeat graph cleanup**")
plot = plot + labs(
    title = ttle ,
    x = "position" , y = "mean coverage per 5 Kb windows") + theme(plot.title = element_markdown(lineheight = 1.5)) 
plot + ylim(0, 150) + geom_hline(yintercept=60, linetype="dashed", color = "red") + scale_color_paletteer_d(nord, aurora)
#ggsave("Before_After_cleanup.PNG")
plot + facet_wrap(~facet, nrow = 2) + ylim(0, 150) + geom_hline(yintercept=60, linetype="dashed", color = "red") + scale_color_paletteer_d(ggpomological, pomological_palette) + theme_pomological_fancy()
```
As you see, I am also using the ggtext package. The problem is that the `theme_pomological_fancy()` cause the "**" in my title to be interpreted as literal "*" and not as a sign "what follow should be in bold".  
I have the feeling if something can be done, it's with the base_theme option but I don't know where to go from there. 

Thank you

EDIT: okay that was easy I needed to specify the title AFTER the use of the pomological theme.
